category_specific_evidence: Issue #3831 notes floating point comparisons in the C code are not NaN safe, and that NaN values could cause the unwrapping code to hang.
PR #8193 adds an implicit NaN mask: any NaNs in the image are treated as masked, computed with np.isnan and combined with any user mask.
The diff sets image_not_masked[nan_mask] = 0 when NaNs are present, so NaN values are replaced before unwrapping rather than propagated.
test_unwrap_3d_nan checks that unwrap_phase on an array with NaNs at masked positions gives the same result as the masked-array version (assert_equal, rng=0).
The PR reports benchmark timings of 34.7 ms on main versus 35.3 ms with the change, and states there is no extra memory cost because a default all-zero mask was already computed.
reproduction_risks: Only NaN is addressed in the passages; +/-inf, signed zero and subnormals are not mentioned.
The C-level floating point comparison fix is not shown in the passages, only the Python-level NaN masking.
The exact NaN-containing input values and array dtype used in the test are not stated beyond the 3D float construction.
